Not sure "art" style matters for sound effects, but mildly realistic I guess?
Description:
So I want my player/character to make footstep sounds as she walks around, and I've got the basic eventing part of that working after following this video:
Again got the actual eventing part done and correct - problem is the RTP "move" sfx files are just really horrible for this. Like the best I was able to do was some kind of very disturbing tap dancing.
Tried googling for footstep sounds for rpg maker - but that all led to posts of people asking how to do it, or plugins that can do it (looked through a few of the plugins and *
best I can tell
* they still require you to already have the sfx you want to use). So I'd love some footstep sound assets I can use or be corrected if one of these plugins already come with the needed sound effects already included. Any help would be appreciated thank you.

Just a normal footstep mostly - maybe one on wood and one on carpet? The big problem with the RTP ones is it's two steps (or more). Biggest problem with the few I've found is there's a bit of steps. I need just one step per file, so it's like one step per square. With two steps in the sfx, at least with the method I've got working right now, it's a lot of stepping sounds at once. Like I said, almost like a weird tap dance. Having just one footstep per sound effect would be helpful there I think.
I'm also open to other ways to do footsteps if this method's too stupid or complex - it's just the first method I stumbled on and I got the actual command stuff working, but I can scrap it if needed.

Edit: Every footstep sfx I find is of multiple steps. Do I need to learn how to edit audio and cut out the bits I want or is there an easier way?

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
That's a pretty basic operation - using Audacity to select everything after the first noise and press delete probably doesn't even require a tutorial? You'll just need to use File -> Export to get the changed sound back out, not File -> Save As.
You can also look for "thump" or things like that, that would probably come singly.
